f.title: Treat overdose, abuse, withdrawal and lack of effect with an OTC drug as adverse events
f.statement: For nonprescription drug serious adverse event reporting, an adverse event is any health-related event associated with the use of a nonprescription drug that is adverse, including an event from an accidental or intentional overdose, an event from abuse of the drug, an event from withdrawal from the drug, and any failure of expected pharmacological action of the drug.
f.applicability: Nonprescription (OTC) drugs marketed in the United States without an approved application (not subject to section 353(b) or 355)

f.title: Apply OTC serious adverse event reporting to nonprescription drugs marketed without an approved application
f.statement: A nonprescription drug, for this section, is a drug that is not subject to section 353(b) (prescription dispensing) and not subject to approval in an application submitted under section 355; the reporting duties of this section apply to such drugs.
f.applicability: Nonprescription (OTC) drugs marketed in the United States without an approved application (not subject to section 353(b) or 355)

Review: OTC drugs marketed under an approved NDA/ANDA (section 355) are outside this section; their adverse event reporting duties sit in 21 CFR 314.80/314.98, not here.

f.title: Classify an OTC adverse event as serious using the statutory outcome criteria
f.statement: A serious adverse event is an adverse event that results in death, a life-threatening experience, inpatient hospitalization, a persistent or significant disability or incapacity, or a congenital anomaly or birth defect, or that requires, based on reasonable medical judgment, a medical or surgical intervention to prevent one of those outcomes.
f.applicability: Nonprescription (OTC) drugs marketed in the United States without an approved application (not subject to section 353(b) or 355)

f.title: Submit to FDA every serious adverse event report received for an OTC drug used in the US, with a copy of the retail label
f.statement: The manufacturer, packer or distributor whose name appears on the label of a nonprescription drug marketed in the United States (the responsible person) must submit to FDA any report it receives of a serious adverse event associated with the drug when used in the United States, together with a copy of the label on or within the retail package.
f.applicability: Nonprescription (OTC) drugs marketed in the United States without an approved application (not subject to section 353(b) or 355)
f.exceptions: FDA may, after notice and comment, exempt reports from (c)(1) and (c)(2) where the exemption would have no adverse effect on public health.

f.title: Retailer named as distributor may authorise the manufacturer or packer to submit reports, if it forwards all adverse events
f.statement: A retailer whose name appears on the label as distributor may, by agreement, authorise the manufacturer or packer of the nonprescription drug to submit the required serious adverse event reports to FDA, provided the retailer directs to that manufacturer or packer all adverse events reported to the retailer through the label address or telephone number required by section 352(x).
f.applicability: Nonprescription (OTC) drugs marketed in the United States without an approved application (not subject to section 353(b) or 355)
f.processes: Partner & vendor oversight; Safety intake & collection

f.title: Submit OTC serious adverse event reports to FDA within 15 business days of receipt
f.statement: The responsible person must submit each serious adverse event report to FDA no later than 15 business days after the report is received through the address or telephone number on the label required by section 352(x).
f.applicability: Nonprescription (OTC) drugs marketed in the United States without an approved application (not subject to section 353(b) or 355)
f.exceptions: FDA may, after notice and comment, establish an exemption where it would have no adverse effect on public health (c)(4).

f.title: Submit new medical information received within 1 year of the initial report within 15 business days
f.statement: The responsible person must submit to FDA any new medical information related to a submitted serious adverse event report that it receives within 1 year of the initial report, no later than 15 business days after it receives the new information.
f.applicability: Nonprescription (OTC) drugs marketed in the United States without an approved application (not subject to section 353(b) or 355)
f.exceptions: Applies only to new medical information received within 1 year of the initial report. FDA may establish an exemption under (c)(4).

f.title: Submit OTC serious adverse event reports on the MedWatch form
f.statement: Each serious adverse event report under this section must be submitted to FDA using the MedWatch form (which FDA may modify for nonprescription drugs), and may be accompanied by additional information.
f.applicability: Nonprescription (OTC) drugs marketed in the United States without an approved application (not subject to section 353(b) or 355)

f.title: Keep records of every adverse event report received for 6 years
f.statement: The responsible person must maintain records related to each report of an adverse event it receives (serious or not) for a period of 6 years.
f.applicability: Nonprescription (OTC) drugs marketed in the United States without an approved application (not subject to section 353(b) or 355)
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Case processing & follow-up

f.title: Give FDA inspectors access to adverse event records
f.statement: During an inspection under section 374, the responsible person must permit an authorized person (a duly designated HHS officer or employee with appropriate credentials) to access the records it must maintain under this section.
f.applicability: Nonprescription (OTC) drugs marketed in the United States without an approved application (not subject to section 353(b) or 355)
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Data integrity & records

f.title: Optionally attach a statement denying that the report admits causation
f.statement: A serious adverse event report (including new medical information) or a voluntary adverse event report submitted to FDA is a safety report under section 379v and may be accompanied by a statement, which becomes part of any publicly released report, denying that the report or the records constitute an admission that the product caused or contributed to the adverse event.
f.applicability: Nonprescription (OTC) drugs marketed in the United States without an approved application (not subject to section 353(b) or 355)
